title: Stabilize MacBookPro13,3 hardware support
author: monomyth
body:
## Summary

Add model-specific hardware support for the 2016 15-inch `MacBookPro13,3`. Wi-Fi and T1 have positive hardware results; the Radeon workaround has a subsequently reproduced failure and remains experimental:

- Install separately calibrated BCM43602 NVRAM so 5 GHz Wi-Fi is available.
- Install package-backed, freeze-safe T1 Touch Bar support.
- Add an experimental Radeon Pro 460 MCLK watchdog: keep VRAM at its highest DPM level while allowing core and PCIe scaling. This passed short tests but did not prevent a later unrecovered GPU hang; it is not a complete stability fix.
- Fix the existing MacBook NVMe suspend workaround so it follows the actual NVMe root device rather than hard-coding PCI `01:00.0`, which is the Radeon on this model.

## Dependencies

This is intentionally a stacked draft:

- Depends on #7671 for the shared atomic BCM43602 NVRAM installer. This branch adds the separate MacBookPro13,3 calibration; it does not widen attachment 290569's model gate.
- Depends on omacom/omarchy-pkgs#298 for `apple-ib-drv-dkms`.

Do not merge this draft until both dependencies land. After #7671 merges, the branch should be rebased onto current `quattro` so the shared dependency commits disappear from this PR.

## Validation correction — 2026-09-05

The short Radeon tests below are historical results, not evidence of sustained stability. On 2026-09-04, with the watchdog service active on `7.2.2-arch1-1-mbp133`, display power was enabled at approximately 17:49:02 PDT. At 17:49:09 the kernel identified OrbbecViewer in a graphics-ring timeout. Reset lost VRAM and failed during SMU firmware reload (`GPU Recovery Failed: -22`). Timeouts continued after the viewer stopped; the host remained SSH-accessible with mostly idle CPUs but blocked graphics work until reboot.

This disproves the earlier blanket claim that the watchdog prevents Radeon hard lockups. It does not isolate a cause among rendering, display-power transitions, watchdog timing, or other driver behavior. The later lid-close/open wake failure also remains unresolved. Keep this PR draft; dependency merges alone are not sufficient for readiness. The newer custom 7.2.3 installation has now been reconciled with the on-host task; its limited validation and separate local changes are described below.

## Additional validation on custom 7.2.3 — 2026-09-05

Live SSH confirms `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133`. The on-host audit verifies installed matching kernel/headers, matching loaded i915/AMDGPU/CS8409/iBridge/Touch Bar modules, and matching canonical/fallback UKIs. These are boot/load/integrity results, not a fresh functional test of every device.

- **Wi-Fi:** a live 5.6 GHz / 80 MHz connection with traffic and the same intended stable local MAC as the 7.2.2 test; reported link rates were 866.6 Mb/s RX and 702 Mb/s TX. This remains MacBookPro13,3-specific evidence.
- **Radeon:** at the September 5 test, the installed apply helper and monitor matched the then-current PR implementation; the subsequent recovery-loop correction is described below. With MCLK pinned at 1270 MHz and the unchanged watchdog active, official OrbbecViewer 2.9.3 used Radeon rendering for Color+Depth at 848x530 / 30 FPS for 60.27 seconds. CPU averaged 36.62% of one logical CPU, peak RSS was 493,522,944 bytes, and no matched GPU/USB/UAS/hung-task/panic/OOM event, coredump or watchdog restart was recorded. The viewer stopped its streams and exited cleanly.
- **Limits:** that one-minute pass does not erase the earlier failure, establish long-term stability, or attribute improvement to the kernel. The earlier software sample used four streams and a different measurement interval; this is not a controlled “8x speedup” result.
- **Intel:** a later Intel-rendered Color+Depth test failed with a blue display and required a power cycle. Retained logs did not establish the unique cause. Intel is disabled in the local Orbbec launcher; no repeat test is proposed.
- **Suspend:** the failed deep/s2idle platform-stage tests and the successful lock/blank/open/unlock containment cycle occurred on 7.2.2. On 7.2.3, only the installed safe-lid policy has been verified so far. This policy avoids kernel suspend and leaves the machine awake when closed, with power/thermal implications; it is not a suspend repair.
- **Separate local work:** the custom kernel forward-port, safe-lid policy, crash-collector repair and Orbbec renderer/scaling changes are not included in this PR. The scoped source comparison found no changes in the compared AMDGPU/i915/ACPI/power paths between the custom source trees; it does not prove all kernel behavior is identical.
- **Subsequent user confirmation:** the owner reported working T1, audio playback, and audio recording/video tested in Zoom on the 7.2.3 setup. This is user-reported functional evidence, not a claim that every individual key or audio mode was retested. Broader controlled Radeon validation is still outstanding. Do not routinely repeat the known-failing platform suspend or Intel camera tests.

### Additional installer issue found during follow-up

This defect was reproduced before the September 7 reconciliation: calling the old stable-MAC helper with an empty or nonexistent machine-id succeeded with the same `02:dd:27:89:9c:fa` result in both cases (isolated helper reproduction; no firmware writes). The old code hashed the salt even when identity was absent. The September 7 update below now rejects this input and adds regression coverage. This reproduction was evidence of a fallback collision, not a two-machine RF test.

## AMDGPU recovery-loop correction — 2026-09-06

OpenAI Codex identified and fixed a second failure mode in the watchdog from retained on-host journal and AMDGPU devcoredump evidence. During an Omarchy screensaver-to-lock transition, the Radeon gfx ring timed out in a Quickshell render thread. The kernel's PCI-config reset then stalled in ATOM BIOS execution and ended with `GPU Recovery Failed: -22`. Once the GPU controls returned `EBUSY`, the watchdog treated every unreadable state as a lost MCLK mask and reran the full apply helper every two seconds. That produced 300 additional gfx timeouts, 301 devcoredumps, and 322 failed MCLK retries before the host was power-cycled.

Commit `fc12fcad` contains the aftermath: DPM reads now distinguish a changed mask from an I/O failure, the apply helper is bounded to ten seconds, and any unreadable control or failed apply stops the watchdog cleanly until its next service start. The pre-display-manager MCLK pin and healthy reset-window monitoring remain unchanged. A focused regression test proves the monitor makes exactly one failed apply attempt and exits successfully instead of entering a retry storm; the complete shell suite reached all tests, with only the four companion-checkout coverage tests unavailable in this isolated worktree.

This contains the failure after it begins; it does not claim to fix the underlying Radeon/ATOM BIOS reset bug. The local safe-lid policy remains required because the same incident was compounded by a later lid-triggered s2idle attempt while Quickshell tasks were already blocked in the failed GPU reset.

## Reconciliation and validation — 2026-09-07

Commit `b58595f2` merges #7671 through `c0fea4e9` without rewriting the existing watchdog history. Both supported model families keep the required `macaddr=` key populated; neither persists the shared firmware placeholder when a unique fallback is needed. MacBookPro13,3 retains its established `mbp133-wifi` salt, while 14,2/14,3 use upstream's `bcm43602-wifi` salt. Existing installed calibration files remain untouched.

The helper now rejects missing, empty, malformed and all-zero machine IDs, propagates hash failures, and validates digest output. Tests cover exact historical addresses, deterministic reruns, distinct IDs, local/unicast bits, no-write failure, migration retry, a missing source MAC key, and rollback after a failed second rename. Cloned machine IDs still produce the same fallback by design; images must initialize distinct machine IDs. No claim of mathematically collision-free addressing is made.

Validation on an isolated Isengard checkout: `bash test/all` passed the CLI suite and **all 190 shell test files**, with the package and ISO companion checkouts. The focused T1 integration suite also passed with the updated #298 package. Tests used temporary firmware/sysfs/service fixtures; no installed Wi-Fi configuration was rewritten and no live radio reload occurred. The original `fc12fcad` watchdog implementation and its recovery-loop regression were preserved.

The on-host task has separately installed a health-gated s2idle policy and recorded a successful controlled cycle on September 6. This supersedes the earlier local no-suspend policy but is **not part of this PR**, not a claim that the underlying Radeon reset problem is fixed, and was not retested during this reconciliation. The custom kernel and other local suspend preparation remain separate work. This PR stays draft pending dependencies, maintainer review and broader stability validation.

## Hardware validation

Test machine:

- MacBookPro13,3, 2016 15-inch
- Intel HD 530 + Apple Radeon Pro 460/Baffin (`1002:67ef`, subsystem `106b:0160`)
- BCM43602 (`14e4:43ba`, subsystem `106b:015a`)
- Apple T1 iBridge (`05ac:8600`)
- Custom Arch `7.2.2-arch1-1-mbp133` kernel for the historical results below
- Omarchy Quattro
- Root filesystem on an external USB SSD; internal Apple NVMe is present but not the boot device

### BCM43602

MacBookPro13,3 uses kernel.org Bugzilla attachment 285753 rather than the 14,2/14,3 attachment in #7671. The installer supplies the host regulatory country and replaces Broadcom's placeholder MAC with a stable locally administered address.

Before: Band 1 only, connected at 2412 MHz.

After:

- Band 2 channels 36–165 available.
- Connected at 5600 MHz/channel 120.
- 866.6 Mbit/s RX and up to 866.6 Mbit/s TX.
- 20/20 gateway pings, zero loss; user speed test normal.

### T1 Touch Bar

- `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-1` package-backed boot passed on the 7.2.2 custom kernel.
- `skip_acpi_power=1`; kernel confirms `ASOC.SOCW(1)` was not executed.
- Esc, volume, brightness, playback, and Fn/F1-F12 controls work.
- iBridge remains in USB configuration 1 with `power/control=on`.
- FaceTime HD camera captured 1280x720 MJPEG and worked in Zoom.
- Internal microphone captured stereo 48 kHz audio.
- DKMS also builds and installs for `6.18.49-1-lts`, but LTS was not boot-tested.

### Radeon

Unrestricted power-state transitions reproduced `VM_CONTEXT` faults and `sdma0`/`sdma1` ring timeouts followed by VRAM loss, SMU reload failure, and unrecoverable blue/black screens. `amdgpu.dpm=0` and `amdgpu.vm_update_mode=1` were not fixes.

Pinning only MCLK at 1270 MHz passed the trigger and repeated-video tests while SCLK returned to 214 MHz at idle. Hyprland resets the mask during session startup, so a fixed 45-second timer left a vulnerable window and reproduced the failure. The final watchdog:

- Applies synchronously before the display manager.
- Polls every 250 ms for the first 90 seconds, then every two seconds.
- Writes only after detecting that the driver reset the mask.
- Restored a simulated reset in 167 ms.
- Caught the real SDDM/session reset before Hyprland startup.
- Passed a 30-second trigger and 3.5-minute soak with zero GPU errors; idle returned to 59 C.

### NVMe targeting

The old service wrote `d3cold_allowed=0` to PCI `01:00.0`. On MacBookPro13,3 that is the Radeon; the internal NVMe is `02:00.0`. The replacement discovers controllers through `/sys/class/nvme` and applies only when the root disk is NVMe. External-USB roots disable and preserve the stale unit instead of touching either device.

## Tests

- `./test/cli` passes.
- All 190 `./test/shell` files pass with the required `omarchy-pkgs` and `omarchy-iso` companion checkouts present.
- New focused suites cover BCM43602 model/source selection, stable placeholder-MAC replacement, T1 production/recovery identities, package ownership, NVMe root-device discovery, exact Radeon board gating, and a simulated compositor MCLK reset.

## Custom 7.2.4 follow-up — 2026-09-15

Additional MacBookPro13,3 validation, with software versions kept separate:

- **Omarchy:** dev package `4.0.0.r2128.gb679363-1` (matching settings package).
- **Linux:** custom `7.2.4-arch1-2-mbp133`, with the existing gmux/VGA arbitration and CS8409 audio patches carried forward. This is not a stock-kernel result, and the custom kernel is not added to this PR.
- **Boot/install checks:** kernel and matching headers installed; canonical/direct UKIs matched, embedded kernel and encrypted external-USB-root command line verified, existing T1/panic add-ons retained, and a 7.2.3 recovery copy preserved. An attended reboot then confirmed the new running release and Hyprland.
- **T1:** unchanged `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-4`, package integrity clean, DKMS rebuild/install successful, iBridge and Touch Bar loaded with matching vermagic and `skip_acpi_power=1`. The owner confirmed Esc/volume keys work.
- **Audio/camera:** patched CS8409 loaded; the owner confirmed audio playback, microphone and camera work after this reboot. This is functional confirmation, not a new resolution/sample-rate or every-mode test.
- **Wi-Fi:** existing 13,3 calibration files remain SHA-256 `a1a13fe89cf570ce94237cd27de36030584e8ec7084c3447c20c4fd668411dba`. Connected at 5600 MHz / 80 MHz; reported RX/TX link rates 866.6/585 Mbit/s, not throughput measurements.
- **Graphics:** watchdog active with zero restarts, manual mode and 1270 MHz MCLK. No matched GPU timeout/reset or storage I/O/Btrfs error in the immediate post-boot check; no failed system/user units.

**Limits:** suspend/resume was not tested on 7.2.4. The separately installed lid-wake DKMS module built for it, but that is not a suspend result. Long-term Radeon stability and controlled display-wake/graphics validation remain outstanding. The prior successful host-local s2idle evidence on 7.2.3 remains historical and outside this PR. Internal-NVMe-root operation was not tested; this host boots an external USB SSD. Keep this PR draft.

Also retaining the separate [13,3 Wi-Fi report from Johann-S](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/7671#issuecomment-5669775431): attachment 290569 with a per-machine MAC and the comment-97 `swctrlmap_2g` edit gave good 5 GHz results on their machine. They did not compare it against 285753 or test a 2.4 GHz join. We have not reproduced that alternative here, so it neither establishes a preferred 13,3 calibration nor validates widening #7671's 14,2/14,3 gate.

No PR code changed and no additional installer fixture tests were run for this update.

+# Shared BCM43602 5 GHz NVRAM helpers for the install leaf and the migration.
+#
+# linux-firmware-broadcom ships the BCM43602 chip firmware but not a board
+# calibration file. Without one, brcmfmac brings the card up with placeholder
+# 5 GHz values (aa5g=1, no per-channel tx-power tables) and only 2.4 GHz
+# networks are visible.
+#
+# The NVRAM is a community dump (kernel.org bugzilla attachment 290569) with
+# ccode=00 / regrev=245, which defers channel legality to the host. Omarchy
+# already persists that from the timezone via set-wireless-regdom.sh. It is
+# calibration for one board, not every Apple BCM43602. MacBookPro14,2 / 14,3
+# use attachment 290569. MacBookPro13,3 uses the separately validated attachment
+# 285753, with its regulatory fields set from the host during installation.
+#
+# Destinations live under /usr/lib/firmware/updates so they override, and do
+# not collide with, linux-firmware-broadcom. A file already at either the
+# override path or the packaged path when this runs wins, user-placed or
+# package-shipped. Once this copy is installed the override path is searched
+# first, so a board file linux-firmware ships later does not replace it.
+
+brcmfmac43602_as_root() {
+  if (( EUID == 0 )); then
+    "$@"
+  else
+    sudo "$@"
+  fi
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_fwdir() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_FWDIR:-/usr/lib/firmware/updates/brcm}"
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_packaged_fwdir() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_PACKAGED_FWDIR:-/usr/lib/firmware/brcm}"
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_nvram_src() {
+  local product default_source
+  product=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_product)
+  if [[ $product == "MacBookPro13,3" ]]; then
+    default_source="${OMARCHY_PATH:-/usr/share/omarchy}/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie-mbp133.txt"
+  else
+    default_source="${OMARCHY_PATH:-/usr/share/omarchy}/default/firmware/apple/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt"
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC43602_NVRAM:-$default_source}"
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_dmi_vendor() {
+  cat "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_VENDOR:-/sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor}" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_dmi_product() {
+  cat "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_DMI_PRODUCT:-/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name}" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_pci_devices() {
+  printf '%s\n' "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_PCI_DEVICES:-/sys/bus/pci/devices}"
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_regdom() {
+  local regdom_file country
+  regdom_file="${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_REGDOM_FILE:-/etc/conf.d/wireless-regdom}"
+  country=$(sed -nE 's/^WIRELESS_REGDOM="?([A-Z]{2})"?$/\1/p' "$regdom_file" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
+  [[ $country =~ ^[A-Z]{2}$ ]] || return 1
+  printf '%s\n' "$country"
+}
+
+# Dual-band BCM43602 (14e4:43ba) on the 2017 Touch Bar MacBook Pros. The 2 GHz
+# only (43bb) and 5 GHz-only (43bc) variants are left alone, as are T2-era
+# chips that already get board files from apple-bcm-firmware.
+brcmfmac43602_needed() {
+  local sys_vendor product
+  sys_vendor=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_vendor)
+  product=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_product)
+  [[ $sys_vendor == Apple* ]] || return 1
+  [[ $product =~ ^MacBookPro(13,3|14,[23])$ ]] || return 1
+  lspci -nn | grep "14e4:43ba" >/dev/null
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_dmi_name() {
+  local vendor product
+  vendor=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_vendor)
+  product=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_product)
+  [[ -n $vendor && -n $product ]] || return 0
+  printf '%s\n' "brcmfmac43602-pcie.${vendor}-${product}.txt"
+}
+
+# Arch compresses everything under /usr/lib/firmware, so a packaged board file
+# arrives as brcmfmac43602-pcie.<dmi>.txt.zst, not under the name the driver
+# asks for. Checking only the plain name would miss it and shadow it anyway.
+brcmfmac43602_installed() {
+  local name dir suffix
+  name=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_name)
+  for dir in "$(brcmfmac43602_fwdir)" "$(brcmfmac43602_packaged_fwdir)"; do
+    for suffix in "" .zst .xz; do
+      [[ -e $dir/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt$suffix ]] && return 0
+      [[ -n $name && -e "$dir/$name$suffix" ]] && return 0
+    done
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+# The NIC bound to 14e4:43ba, not the first wireless interface in glob order
+# (a USB adapter at install time would otherwise donate its address). The
+# wiphy's macaddress is the permanent address; net/*/address is whatever is
+# current, which NetworkManager randomises while scanning. 00:90:4c is the
+# Broadcom OUI, not a board identity, so it is not substituted in — install
+# then writes a per-machine locally-administered address instead of the dump
+# donor. The macaddr= key still has to exist in the file: without it, BCM43602
+# firmware times out on cur_etheraddr and crashes the dongle (MacBookPro14,3).
+brcmfmac43602_wifi_mac() {
+  local bdf pci_devices candidate mac
+  pci_devices=$(brcmfmac43602_pci_devices)
+  bdf=$(lspci -Dnn | awk '/14e4:43ba/ { if (!found) { print $1; found=1 } }')
+  [[ -n $bdf ]] || return 1
+  for candidate in "$pci_devices/$bdf"/ieee80211/phy*/macaddress "$pci_devices/$bdf"/net/*/address; do
+    mac=$(cat "$candidate" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    [[ $mac =~ ^([0-9a-fA-F]{2}:){5}[0-9a-fA-F]{2}$ ]] || continue
+    if [[ ${mac,,} == 00:90:4c:* ]]; then
+      return 1
+    fi
+    printf '%s\n' "$mac"
+    return 0
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+brcmfmac43602_machine_id() {
+  cat "${OMARCHY_BRCMFMAC_MACHINE_ID:-/etc/machine-id}" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+# Stable locally-administered unicast address for this installation. Keep the
+# established 13,3 salt so an existing installation does not change identity.
+# Cloned machine IDs produce the same address: images must generate a fresh ID.
+brcmfmac43602_stable_mac() {
+  local id seed salt
+  id=$(brcmfmac43602_machine_id)
+  [[ $id =~ ^[0-9a-f]{32}$ && $id != 00000000000000000000000000000000 ]] || return 1
+  if [[ $(brcmfmac43602_dmi_product) == "MacBookPro13,3" ]]; then
+    salt=mbp133-wifi
+  else
+    salt=bcm43602-wifi
+  fi
+  seed=$(printf '%s' "$id:$salt" | sha256sum) || return 1
+  [[ $seed =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}[[:space:]] ]] || return 1
+  seed=${seed:0:10}
+  printf '02:%s:%s:%s:%s:%s\n' \
+    "${seed:0:2}" "${seed:2:2}" "${seed:4:2}" "${seed:6:2}" "${seed:8:2}"
+}
+
+# Reloading brcmfmac here would drop a live Wi-Fi connection, including the
+# one carrying an update. Callers must not wrap this in `if`; bash would then
+# disable errexit for the body and a failed install would look like success.
+#
+# Both names are staged under temporary names and renamed into place together.
+# A write that fails part-way (ENOSPC truncates its destination) must not leave
+# a partial file under the name the driver loads, where brcmfmac43602_installed
+# would keep it forever and the migration would never ask for the reboot.
+brcmfmac43602_install() {
+  local src fwdir mac work name target product country
+  local -a targets sed_args
+
+  src=$(brcmfmac43602_nvram_src)
+  [[ -f $src ]] || return 1
+
+  fwdir=$(brcmfmac43602_fwdir)
+  targets=("$fwdir/brcmfmac43602-pcie.txt")
+  name=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_name)
+  if [[ -n $name ]]; then
+    targets+=("$fwdir/$name")
+  fi
+
+  work=$(mktemp) || return 1
+  product=$(brcmfmac43602_dmi_product)
+  # Preserve the required key, substituting a real address or a stable fallback.
+  # Stripping macaddr crashes 14,3 firmware; retaining the shared default is not
+  # a unique identity. Refuse installation if neither source is usable.
+  if mac=$(brcmfmac43602_wifi_mac); then
+    sed_args=(-e "s/^macaddr=.*/macaddr=$mac/")
+  elif mac=$(brcmfmac43602_stable_mac); then
+    sed_args=(-e "s/^macaddr=.*/macaddr=$mac/")
+  else
+    echo "Cannot install BCM43602 NVRAM without a usable MAC or machine-id" >&2
+    rm -f "$work"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  if [[ $product == "MacBookPro13,3" ]]; then
+    country=$(brcmfmac43602_regdom) || {
+      echo "Cannot install MacBookPro13,3 BCM43602 NVRAM without a wireless regulatory country" >&2
+      rm -f "$work"
+      return 1
+    }
+    sed_args+=(-e "s/^ccode=.*/ccode=$country/" -e 's/^regrev=.*/regrev=0/')
+  fi
+
+  if ! grep -q '^macaddr=' "$src" || ! sed "${sed_args[@]}" "$src" >"$work"; then
+    rm -f "$work"
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  if ! brcmfmac43602_as_root mkdir -p "$fwdir"; then
+    rm -f "$work"
+    return 1
+  fi
+  for target in "${targets[@]}"; do
+    if ! brcmfmac43602_as_root install -m 644 "$work" "$target.tmp"; then
+      brcmfmac43602_as_root rm -f "${targets[@]/%/.tmp}"
+      rm -f "$work"
+      return 1
+    fi
+  done
+  rm -f "$work"
+  for target in "${targets[@]}"; do
+    if ! brcmfmac43602_as_root mv -f "$target.tmp" "$target"; then
+      brcmfmac43602_as_root rm -f "${targets[@]}" "${targets[@]/%/.tmp}"
+      return 1
+    fi
+  done
+}

+if brcmfmac43602_needed && ! brcmfmac43602_installed; then

+fi

+# MacBookPro13,3's Radeon Pro 460 can hard-lock during VRAM clock transitions.
+# Keep every core and PCIe level available while pinning only VRAM to its
+# highest DPM level. Hyprland's initial modeset resets the mask, so a lightweight
+# monitor reapplies it immediately and keeps guarding later session transitions.
+product_file="${OMARCHY_MBP133_DMI_PRODUCT:-/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name}"
+pci_devices="${OMARCHY_MBP133_PCI_DEVICES:-/sys/bus/pci/devices}"
+product_name=$(cat "$product_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
+gpu_found=0
+
+if [[ $product_name == "MacBookPro13,3" ]]; then
+  for candidate in "$pci_devices"/*; do
+    [[ -f $candidate/vendor && -f $candidate/device ]] || continue
+    if [[ $(<"$candidate/vendor") == 0x1002 && \
+          $(<"$candidate/device") == 0x67ef && \
+          $(<"$candidate/subsystem_vendor") == 0x106b && \
+          $(<"$candidate/subsystem_device") == 0x0160 ]]; then
+      gpu_found=1
+      break
+    fi
+  done
+fi
+
+if (( gpu_found == 1 )); then
+  echo "Detected MacBookPro13,3 Radeon Pro 460; pinning the VRAM clock"
+
+  helper_source="$OMARCHY_INSTALL/hardware/apple/mbp133-amdgpu-stability"
+  monitor_source="$OMARCHY_INSTALL/hardware/apple/mbp133-amdgpu-stability-monitor"
+  helper_target="${OMARCHY_MBP133_HELPER:-/etc/omarchy/hardware/mbp133-amdgpu-stability}"
+  monitor_target="${OMARCHY_MBP133_MONITOR:-/etc/omarchy/hardware/mbp133-amdgpu-stability-monitor}"
+  unit_file="${OMARCHY_MBP133_UNIT:-/etc/systemd/system/omarchy-mbp133-amdgpu-stability.service}"
+  timer_file="${OMARCHY_MBP133_TIMER:-/etc/systemd/system/omarchy-mbp133-amdgpu-stability.timer}"
+
+  sudo install -D -m 0755 "$helper_source" "$helper_target"
+  sudo install -D -m 0755 "$monitor_source" "$monitor_target"
+  {
+    echo '[Unit]'

+
+[[ $(cat "$dmi_product" 2>/dev/null || true) == "MacBookPro13,3" ]] || exit 0
+
+gpu=""
+for candidate in "$pci_devices"/*; do
+  [[ -f $candidate/vendor && -f $candidate/device ]] || continue
+  [[ $(<"$candidate/vendor") == 0x1002 ]] || continue
+  [[ $(<"$candidate/device") == 0x67ef ]] || continue
+  [[ $(<"$candidate/subsystem_vendor") == 0x106b ]] || continue
+  [[ $(<"$candidate/subsystem_device") == 0x0160 ]] || continue
+  gpu=$candidate
+  break
+done
+[[ -n $gpu ]] || exit 0
+
+stop_after_io_failure() {
+  local detail=$1
+  local message="Radeon DPM controls are unavailable ($detail); stopping the watchdog until its next service start to avoid a GPU recovery retry storm"
+  logger -t mbp133-amdgpu-stability "$message"
+  printf '%s\n' "$message" >&2
+  exit 0
+}
+
+read_control() {
+  local path=$1 value
+  if ! IFS= read -r value <"$path"; then
+    return 1
+  fi
+  printf '%s\n' "$value"
+}
+
+mclk_is_highest() {
+  local contents line level highest="" active=""
+
+  contents=$(cat "$gpu/pp_dpm_mclk") || return 2
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    if [[ $line =~ ^[[:space:]]*([0-9]+): ]]; then
+      level=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
+      highest=$level
+      [[ $line == *'*'* ]] && active=$level
+    fi
+  done <<<"$contents"
+
+  [[ -n $highest && $active == "$highest" ]]
+}
+
+started=${SECONDS:-0}
+while true; do
+  force=$(read_control "$gpu/power_dpm_force_performance_level") || \
+    stop_after_io_failure "cannot read power_dpm_force_performance_level"
+
+  mclk_status=0
+  mclk_is_highest || mclk_status=$?
+  (( mclk_status == 2 )) && stop_after_io_failure "cannot read pp_dpm_mclk"
+
+  if [[ $force != "manual" ]] || (( mclk_status != 0 )); then
+    if timeout --kill-after=2s "${apply_timeout}s" "$apply_helper"; then
+      logger -t mbp133-amdgpu-stability "Reapplied the highest MCLK mask after its state changed"
+    else
+      stop_after_io_failure "the MCLK apply helper failed"
+    fi
+  fi
+
+  if (( SECONDS - started < 90 )); then
+    sleep 0.25
+  else
+    sleep 2
+  fi
+done

Validation correction: the Radeon watchdog is not a complete stability fix. I have updated the PR description and am keeping it draft.

On the previously tested custom Linux 7.2.2 kernel, with the watchdog service active, the display was powered on at approximately 17:49:02 PDT on September 4. The recorded kernel sequence was:

```text
17:49:09 ring gfx timeout, signaled seq=287584, emitted seq=287586
17:49:09 Process OrbbecViewer pid 48351 thread OrbbecView:cs0 pid 48360
17:49:10 VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!
17:49:14 SMU load firmware failed
17:49:14 GPU Recovery Failed: -22
```

Timeouts persisted after the viewer stopped. SSH survived, but graphics work and process-enumeration probes became stuck; reboot was needed. This directly limits the earlier short trigger/soak results. It does not prove a root cause among the display transition, rendering, watchdog timing or other driver behavior.

The machine's owner now reports Linux 7.2.3 and additional host-side optimizations. I am collecting their exact changes and validation results; neither the version bump nor app-only software rendering should be presented as a Radeon fix. The historical Wi-Fi/T1 results remain identified as 7.2.2 results, and LTS remains build-only.

Before readiness we need controlled display-wake/lid and graphics validation on the exact proposed configuration, with usable crash capture and no concurrent workloads. The latest shared-installer changes in #7671 also need reconciliation rather than retaining this branch's older 14,3 missing-MAC stripping behavior. No new hardware tests or code changes are claimed in this update.


**Update after coordination with the on-host task:** live custom `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133`, matching module/UKI verification and a live 5.6 GHz link are confirmed. The description now includes the 60.27-second Radeon Color+Depth test (848x530 / 30 FPS, 36.62% of one CPU, clean exit), under the byte-identical PR watchdog. This is not sustained stability or a controlled speedup comparison. Intel later failed and is disabled. The safe lid cycle and failed platform-suspend tests were on 7.2.2; 7.2.3 has policy verification, not a new physical lid-cycle result.

The description also records an isolated installer defect reproduced in this follow-up: empty and nonexistent machine-id inputs both produce `02:dd:27:89:9c:fa` successfully. Input handling/tests and the updated #7671 base need reconciliation before merge. No installer, kernel, GPU or power configuration was changed in this PR follow-up.

Pushed `b58595f2`: reconciled #7671 through `c0fea4e9`, preserving the 13,3 `mbp133-wifi` identity salt and the existing `fc12fcad` watchdog correction. Missing/empty/malformed/all-zero machine IDs now fail without leaving firmware files; hash failures are propagated. Existing installed calibration is preserved. Added exact-address, repeatability, invalid-input, migration-retry, required-key and second-rename rollback coverage.

Validation on an isolated Isengard checkout: CLI suite and all 190 shell test files passed with companion repositories present. The final T1 integration test also passed against package #298's updated recipe. No live Wi-Fi reload, installed firmware change, suspend test or GPU reset was performed. The owner's T1/audio/Zoom confirmation is now included in the description. Still draft: underlying Radeon stability and dependency publication remain separate requirements.

## Custom 7.2.4 follow-up — 2026-09-15

Additional MacBookPro13,3 validation, with software versions kept separate:

- **Omarchy:** dev package `4.0.0.r2128.gb679363-1` (matching settings package).
- **Linux:** custom `7.2.4-arch1-2-mbp133`, with the existing gmux/VGA arbitration and CS8409 audio patches carried forward. This is not a stock-kernel result, and the custom kernel is not added to this PR.
- **Boot/install checks:** kernel and matching headers installed; canonical/direct UKIs matched, embedded kernel and encrypted external-USB-root command line verified, existing T1/panic add-ons retained, and a 7.2.3 recovery copy preserved. An attended reboot then confirmed the new running release and Hyprland.
- **T1:** unchanged `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-4`, package integrity clean, DKMS rebuild/install successful, iBridge and Touch Bar loaded with matching vermagic and `skip_acpi_power=1`. The owner confirmed Esc/volume keys work.
- **Audio/camera:** patched CS8409 loaded; the owner confirmed audio playback, microphone and camera work after this reboot. This is functional confirmation, not a new resolution/sample-rate or every-mode test.
- **Wi-Fi:** existing 13,3 calibration files remain SHA-256 `a1a13fe89cf570ce94237cd27de36030584e8ec7084c3447c20c4fd668411dba`. Connected at 5600 MHz / 80 MHz; reported RX/TX link rates 866.6/585 Mbit/s, not throughput measurements.
- **Graphics:** watchdog active with zero restarts, manual mode and 1270 MHz MCLK. No matched GPU timeout/reset or storage I/O/Btrfs error in the immediate post-boot check; no failed system/user units.

**Limits:** suspend/resume was not tested on 7.2.4. The separately installed lid-wake DKMS module built for it, but that is not a suspend result. Long-term Radeon stability and controlled display-wake/graphics validation remain outstanding. The prior successful host-local s2idle evidence on 7.2.3 remains historical and outside this PR. Internal-NVMe-root operation was not tested; this host boots an external USB SSD. Keep this PR draft.

Also retaining the separate [13,3 Wi-Fi report from Johann-S](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/7671#issuecomment-5669775431): attachment 290569 with a per-machine MAC and the comment-97 `swctrlmap_2g` edit gave good 5 GHz results on their machine. They did not compare it against 285753 or test a 2.4 GHz join. We have not reproduced that alternative here, so it neither establishes a preferred 13,3 calibration nor validates widening #7671's 14,2/14,3 gate.

No PR code changed and no additional installer fixture tests were run for this update.

`b83e57f6` closes a gap in the Radeon watchdog's failure containment. The monitor already bounded reapply calls and stopped after failure, but the service's initial `ExecStartPre` called the helper directly and `Restart=on-failure` could repeat a failed startup.

The initial apply now uses `timeout --kill-after=2s 10s`; the unit has `TimeoutStartSec=15s`, `TimeoutStopSec=5s` and `Restart=no`. Initial failure stops the attempt rather than automatically retrying against an unhealthy GPU. The mask is still applied before the display manager, and healthy session-time monitoring is unchanged. These are userspace bounds, not a promise that signals can recover a task stuck uninterruptibly inside a failed kernel GPU operation.

All 11 focused Radeon fixture checks passed, including the actual generated startup command with a failing helper and a stalled helper. The timeout fixture terminates before the service-level deadline. Shell syntax and `git diff --check` pass. The tests use temporary files/stubs; no live GPU writes, service changes, suspend or forced-reset tests were performed on Isengard, and the full Omarchy suite was not rerun for this small follow-up.

This does not fix the underlying Radeon reset/SMU failure. The PR remains draft with its existing hardware-validation and dependency limits. NVMe targeting and T1/T2 resume scope were deliberately not changed by this follow-up.
